findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no soap to be available at kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with soap.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer to be available in cooler. Discussed with PIC, thermometer was brought and placed in cooler. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer available.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed can opener to be soiled with black mold. Discussed with PIC, can opener was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure can opener is being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed food handlers licenses to be missing for multiple members of staff. Discussed with PIC, staff will completed food handlers training. Ensure all food handling staff have a valid food handlers license available within the facility during hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed multiple dented cans to be present in dry storage area. Discussed with PIC, cans were pulled and will be discarded. Ensure facility is checking for dented cans at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of milk and multiple containers of nuts to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper dates marking practices. Dates were placed on the milk, and the bags of nuts were discarded. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple food items to be stored on the floor in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, items will be moved to an approved location. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed shelving unit in dish room to have plates not inverted with no proper covering available. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper equipment/utensil storage. Plates and utensils were run through dish machine, and were then returned to shelf in an inverted manner. Ensure any equipment/utensil being stored in a shelving unit is either covered or inverted to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed 2 sanitizer buckets to be at a concentration of 50 ppm Quat. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer buckets were dumped and remade and tested to be 200 ppm Quat. Ensure all sanitizer buckets are prepared at the proper sanitation level and are being replaced roughly every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the lobby juice dispenser nozzles to be soiled with juice splash/buildup. Discussed with PIC, nozzles will be removed and put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination/buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair to the right of the dish machine and at the mop sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents caulking from getting damaged.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed a member of staff put on gloves without washing hands before. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper glove wear. Staff member rewashed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no paper towels to be present at one of the kitchen hand sinks. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand washing sink. Ensure all hand washing sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of ham located in walk in cooler to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, ham was discarded and education was provided on proper date marking procedure. Ensure all TCS foods kept past their 7 day date marking maximum are discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair to the right of the dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents caulking from getting damaged.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a bottle of oven cleaner to be in contact with clean utensils. Discussed with PIC, bottle was relocated and utensils in contact were pulled to be sanitized. Ensure chemicals are kept out of contact with food contact surfaces, and are not being stored on the same shelving as utensils.
findings.citation_text: 7-301.11 Separation. POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed ice scoop to be resting in between ice machine and cooler. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was moved to a sanitized tray. Ensure ice scoop is being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed 2 mops to be resting in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mops were moved to strainer part of mop bucket. Ensure mops are being stored in a way that allows them to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
